dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: They locked the manual bypass. We can't clear the heat if the main vent overloads.

dialogueInline.speaker: PARENT
dialogueInline.text: We've got people living on these terraces. How long until it gets too hot?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Depends how long the main stack holds.

dialogueInline.speaker: PARENT
dialogueInline.text: That's a terrible answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: It's the only accurate one.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: Why can't they just turn the vents back on?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Somebody's locked the controls from above.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: The people who built it?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: No. The people who have the key.

panelPlan: SHATTERFORGE. Beneath the industrial exhaust route, families carry laundry and small children through maintenance terraces while the great service vents cycle.
The parent begins carrying supplies down the service stairs. A little boy keeps looking up at the great exhaust structure; he has slept beneath it.
Abby hears them. She asks the worker to show her the local bypass. A red manual release has been sealed under an authority cover; the plate still shows tool.

sourceActionBeats: *SHATTERFORGE. Beneath the industrial exhaust route, families carry laundry and small children through maintenance terraces while the great service vents cycle overhead. The alarms mean work rather than danger—until the vents fail to answer their controls.*

*The parent begins carrying supplies down the service stairs. A little boy keeps looking up at the great exhaust structure; he has slept beneath it his whole life and has never thought of it as a weapon.*

*Abby hears them. She asks the worker to show her the local bypass. A red manual release has been sealed under an authority cover; the plate still shows tool marks from the last maintenance inspection. She takes a photograph of the actual mechanism and its status, not a staged accusation against an unnamed faction.*

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: When was the last successful vent cycle?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Early morning. Then we lost remote release. The machine itself still answers the local checks.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Keep the inspection crew here. I need the people who can tell me what the machinery actually does when we free it.

dialogueInline.speaker: PARENT
dialogueInline.text: Are you going to make them let us leave?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I can keep a route clear for your family. I can't promise they'll stop trying to close another one. Pack what the children can carry. The rest can wait for us to come back for it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: The manual vent was locked from outside the service system. Who ordered it?

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: The evacuation plan requires a single controlled departure.

panelPlan: The parent looks toward the apartment and chooses the medicine case instead of a heavier trunk. It is not a triumphant decision.
Abby arrives as Fear's emissary announces that families must board Triarch-controlled transports. She watches the worker try a local release and discover the.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The parent looks toward the apartment and chooses the medicine case instead of a heavier trunk. It is not a triumphant decision.*
*Abby arrives as Fear's emissary announces that families must board Triarch-controlled transports. She watches the worker try a local release and discover the deliberate lock.*

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: It requires you to make people leave in the ships you've chosen. You've disabled the way they could stay while we move them safely.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: Those are the available transports.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Not anymore. We have other ships. And you're going to find out how many.

panelPlan: Abby looks beyond him to the families who were using the terraces as homes, not as bargaining counters.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Abby looks beyond him to the families who were using the terraces as homes, not as bargaining counters.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK / AURIC — CIVILIAN RESPONSE

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Someone who paid to turn our market into a funeral pyre bought control relays for those vents. Same route through the accounts. Not the same person on the receipt.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: That's not enough to accuse the Triarch in public.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: No. It's enough to tell people not to trust the vents to behave innocently.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We have to accept the ships before the berths are ready. If we tell them to wait, they'll wait under a furnace.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We've still got families in the freight hall from Tal Corvus.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then ask which ones can help us make room. Don't turn their survival last month into a reason to refuse someone else today.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: You always know how to make a simple refusal sound impossible.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: The simple ones are usually wrong.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK keeps the civilian corridor open. At Auric, Halev is still repairing the market fire when Naomi brings warning of another evacuation. Jex.
Halev looks exhausted by the truth of it.
They begin clearing arrivals space with no promise that the shelter problem will disappear.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — BROKEN OATH APPROACH

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Captain, we're across their departure path. The service plume's shifted again.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: Move the forward camera. I want the whole civilian line behind us.

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: That's not a course correction.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: I know what a course correction is.

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Then I'm asking you for one.

panelPlan: Broken Oath holds an approach position where its broadcast cameras can see the evacuees. The same hull blocks two loaded civilian skiffs.
Pike looks at the famous image he has arranged and the ugly traffic geometry behind it. He delays moving. His choice will matter physically later.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — ASHFANG APPROACH

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We could force them into the Triarch docking line.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Back off.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We have room for another pass.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: They don't. Back off now.

panelPlan: Ashfang uses engine wash to threaten the evacuation approach. A loaded skiff is driven dangerously toward a support frame. Billie sees the family shapes behind.
The engines fall away. The skiff clears by a narrow margin. Billie watches its pilot regain a stable course. She remembers the medical freighter and refuses to.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — LOWER RUNS

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: He said he'd be five minutes. I know everyone says that. But he meant it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: People who go into maintenance runs always mean it. They just forget time is allowed to pass while they're looking at a problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: Can you get someone in after him?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I've got a search crew at the lower hatch. They won't leave until I tell them it's physically impossible to go farther. I won't say that while the route's still open.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Your evacuation margin is narrowing, Tess.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I know. I'm getting the skiffs out while the crew checks the route. I'll tell you when I need help.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: What did Arun take with him?

panelPlan: Shatterforge lower runs. Tess has been directing evacuation skiffs when a resident reports that her husband Arun went to check a manual heat route and has not.
The resident is still staring into the lower run. Tess can see the woman's hands are badly burned from a failed attempt to open the maintenance hatch.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

*The resident is still staring into the lower run. Tess can see the woman's hands are badly burned from a failed attempt to open the maintenance hatch.*
sourceScene: SCENE 5 — THE HUSBAND IN THE VENTS (P11)

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: His service kit. The little diagnostic slate. He said the bypass wasn't answering and he could find out why before the families started to panic.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Can he work the manual release?

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: He knows the vent. He's kept it alive since before we had enough people to staff the night shift. He gets angry with it. Talks to it like an old friend who's disappointed him.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That sounds like half my crew. All right. The search team has his route and his tools. They know where he might have stopped to investigate instead of coming back.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You can't keep a ship waiting for my husband.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'm not. I'm keeping the route open while people who know the machinery search for him. There's a difference. And you can help me by moving to the staging berth, so I don't have another person to look for.

panelPlan: The woman does not move immediately. Tess waits without turning the moment into a public announcement. Finally she takes the woman's uninjured hand and helps.
The resident watches Tess send one more family to the waiting craft before turning back to the missing man's location. The rescue and search are simultaneous.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — CROWN VENT

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: We can anchor over the crown and absorb the plume, but there's no guarantee we can hold enough power after the bypass opens.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: How long?

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: Until the shield fails. I'd rather not give you a number you'll mistake for a promise.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You and I are having a very similar day.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I've got the crown vent. Once we shield it, you can open the manual relief.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You can't sit there indefinitely.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I don't intend to. Do your work quickly.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Abby—

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I know why you're doing it. I'm not thanking you yet.

panelPlan: Scythe of Saville can shield the crown vent if Tess opens the manual bypass, redirecting hot discharge away from the inhabited terraces. The maneuver may.
She calls Tess.
Tess has already looked at Scythe's shield geometry. She knows the size of the ship and the length of time a working radiator can tolerate this discharge. She.

sourceActionBeats: *Scythe of Saville can shield the crown vent if Tess opens the manual bypass, redirecting hot discharge away from the inhabited terraces. The maneuver may destroy Scythe's protective field and strand its crew. Abby chooses it with open eyes.*

sourceScene: SCENE 6 — THE SHIELD OVER THE VENT (P12–P14)

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: That's fortunate. I'm going to be busy.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Your port shield's been run hard since the last crossing. Do you have the actual temperature, or is someone giving you the one that makes the decision easier?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You heard him.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I did. I'm still opening the bypass. But if you get enough time to pull away, you take it. You don't keep a ship over a vent because a captain thinks she's supposed to be brave.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I know what my crew can tolerate.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You're not the only one who knows them. I've eaten at their table. Don't make me go through every name to remind you they're people.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Get the families out. Let me do my part without arguing me into a worse decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I know. I want to see you after, too. You can complain to me about the repairs. In person. Now get the families off the lower terraces.

panelPlan: Abby looks to engineering and repeats the question without softening it. The engineer gives the less comforting measurement.
Tess closes the channel with an acknowledgement, not a farewell. She goes back to the bypass controls and gives the next instruction.
Scythe settles into the only physically viable shield position, maintaining the hull silhouette and directional scale of a major Shard vessel.

summary: WHOSE SHIP IS IN THE WAY (P15–P16) — 1/2

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — BROKEN OATH

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: We should pull back now.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIKE
dialogueInline.text: If we leave, the record makes her the only captain who stood between the heat and the civilians.

dialogueInline.speaker: PILOT
dialogueInline.text: It's a record, Captain. It won't care where our hull is after it melts.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: They locked the release to herd people into their transports. We were told the service vents were damaged.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: You still have a command channel to the Triarch.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Send them the record. Tell them I'm not going to stop the people leaving on independent skiffs.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: You'll be called a traitor.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: They can call me when they've finished lying about what they did.

panelPlan: Pike notices Scythe's rescue in his camera feed. The rising plume will reach Broken Oath's exposed position.
He delays once again. On Ashfang, Billie receives the authenticated Fear-mask vent lock order.
The tactical officer keeps a hand on the unanswered Triarch channel. He has sailed with Billie long enough to know a dramatic refusal can be followed by a very.

summary: WHOSE SHIP IS IN THE WAY (P15–P16) — 2/2

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: The tanker contracts are still theirs. If they cancel them, we'll be three watches from the nearest fuel berth that will take us.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then start counting the watches.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We have people who will leave the ship if we can't feed them.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I know. You've been the one signing the ration orders. I don't imagine you needed me to explain that.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Then what exactly did we win by refusing?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Nothing we can eat. Nothing we can sell. We stopped making it worse for people who were already in trouble. I don't want that turned into a glorious victory, either.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: That's going to be a hard speech for the crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then don't make a speech. Tell them what we did, what it cost, and where the fuel's going to come from. I need to decide that last part before anyone starts congratulating me.

panelPlan: Billie considers the evacuation craft escaping beneath her hull. She can see the child she nearly forced into the frame; her ship's wash is still scattering.
He returns to work. Billie watches the opened evacuation route and begins contacting independent suppliers who may demand payment she doesn't have.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — EVACUATION ROUTE

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: That's him! That's Arun!

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Help them aboard. Keep moving. We've got three skiffs left.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: We have about a minute at this load.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Tell Tess.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: She's clearing the first two.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then hold until she's got them clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: The last one's stuck. I'm going back in.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You're not taking Gravefire inside that plume.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No, I'm using the tug. We can tow them if the line holds.

panelPlan: Tess opens the manual bypass. The plume rises into Scythe's shield. A search team returns from the lower runs with Arun alive. Three skiffs remain trapped at.
On Scythe, power margins collapse toward the engineering limit.
Gravefire draws the first two out. The third has a damaged drive mount.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: There isn't time to make it safe.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I know. I'd appreciate it if you'd spend the remaining time keeping the roof on.

panelPlan: Abby almost laughs. Scythe continues shielding. One of the most important choices of the story is made without anyone becoming eloquent.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHATTERFORGE — THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: The skiff's exposed. Scythe is losing her field. We can reach one with a shield turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Commodore, those are the limits of the maneuver. I won't give you a second option by pretending this ship can do something she can't.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Cover the civilian skiff.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Understood. Helm, bring us around. Shields to the skiff.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You've got the original lock record?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Confirmed.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Abby, the last skiff is clear. Now get yourself out.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: We're going to try.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: The outer shield emitter's losing its phase reference. If we retract now, there's a chance the tether survives.

panelPlan: Thunderbreak can extend shield protection to either the last civilian skiff or Scythe's damaged hull, but not both with the available geometry and power.
Broken Oath takes the plume it remained positioned beneath. Pike abandons his lost broadcast and withdraws the scorched ship. On Scythe, Abby hears.
Inside Scythe, the engineering team has made every practical preparation for a tether release. None of the displays suggests an easy escape.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: The skiff hasn't cleared. Hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: Captain, I need an answer before the reference goes entirely. If the field collapses while we're anchored, we may never get a second release.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: When Tess says clear, we release. Not when you think the skiff ought to be clear. When she says it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEER
dialogueInline.text: I have family on this ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: So do I. I'm sorry.

panelPlan: Abby looks at the tiny freighter climbing away from the dock mouth on Gravefire's tow. The numbers are just barely improving.
She lets him return to his console rather than asking him to forgive her. Gravefire's confirmation arrives just as the emitter begins to arc. Scythe.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: GRAVEFIRE — BRIDGE — AFTER EVACUATION

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Don't tell me you came to apologize.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I came to see what you have.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: A last known vector, a broken tether, and two captains who've volunteered to look. Less than I had an hour ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I can assign another search vessel when the civilian lane clears.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That's generous. Will the lane ever clear?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I don't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You had a choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: People keep reminding me the skiff had families aboard. I've met them. One woman pressed her child's coat into my hands because she couldn't find a way to thank me. I helped her put it back on the child. I don't need a lesson about who was on that skiff.

sourceActionBeats: *Gravefire's bridge, after the civilian survivors are safely docked. Tess has been watching the last known vector for Scythe. Venn comes aboard when the search crews have moved to the outer sector.*

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't going to give you one.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Good. Because I know why you did it, and I hate you for it anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That's what I can't stand. If you'd been stupid, if you'd mistaken the range, if somebody had lied about the shield, I could spend the next year proving it. But you saw both ships. You knew who was on them.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I did.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Abby would have made the same choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I think so.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Don't do that. Don't make her agree with you before we've found her.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You're right.

panelPlan: Venn doesn't move.

sourceActionBeats: *Venn doesn't move.*
*The pause stretches. Tess looks at Scythe's last vector.*

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: When we were little, Abby used to climb the cooling frames. She'd get halfway across and freeze, too proud to ask me to come after her. I'd sit on the ground and insult her until she got angry enough to move. Worked every time.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: What would you call her now?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Every name I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Keep it open. If somebody hears anything—scrap, a beacon, a burst that isn't even a signal—I want it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You will have it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: And don't bring me a death notice because someone's decided the search is inconvenient.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I won't.
